subject: Re: Partner rev-share: milestone-tied payments, lead ownership & technical acceptance
messages:
From: Ellen Harper <ellen.harper@skyline-analytics.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Paul Jensen <paul.jensen@sysint.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partner rev-share discussion: integration milestones & lead pathing

Hi Neha / Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Skyline is excited about embedding Redwood as the inference layer for our SmartInsights product. Paul and I sketched a pragmatic commercial approach so we can move to a pilot quickly:

- 60/40 rev-share (Skyline/Redwood) on net subscription revenue for the first 12 months post-go-live for customers where Skyline is the primary introducer;
- Staged platform payments tied to integration milestones: 25% on contract signature, 35% on production API integration (our integration tests pass), 40% on go-live (first paying customer onboarded);
- Lead registration: Skyline requests lead protection for 90 days from first intro, with a standard validation checklist;
- Technical acceptance: integration approval is based on an agreed test suite (we can share our CI tests) and SLAs around latency on sample workloads.

I've attached a draft SOW and a simple lead-registration matrix to show how we'd flag intros. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept milestone-tied payments and the proposed lead window? Also — are there carve-outs if Redwood brings an existing Skyline target into the opportunity?

Regards,
Ellen
VP Partnerships | Skyline Analytics
[Attachment: Skyline_Proposed_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: lead-registration-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Ellen Harper <ellen.harper@skyline-analytics.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partner rev-share discussion: integration milestones & lead pathing

Ellen — thanks for the clear outline and the SOW. Quick acknowledge and some high-level comments from Redwood:

1) Staged payments: Redwood can accept milestone-linked disbursements, but we need clear acceptance criteria per milestone in the SOW. For example:
   - Signature: legal sign-off on MOU/SOW and PO (25%)
   - Prod API integration: our automated integration harness passes the shared test suite for 48 hours without regressions (35%)
   - Go-live: first paid customer successfully invoiced and live for 30 days (40%)

2) Lead registration: 90 days is reasonable for inbound introductions where Skyline is the originator and hands off directly to Redwood sales. We propose: 1) registration via HubSpot form (link below), 2) single point-of-contact at Skyline, and 3) a 14-day rebuttal window for Redwood to flag prior engagement.

3) Carve-outs: Redwood will not pay rev-share on accounts where Redwood had a documented active engagement (qualified opportunity) in our CRM within the prior 6 months. We can add a ‘prior engagement’ check in the lead matrix.

I've looped in Marissa (revenue ops) to propose the commission cadence and Camila to align on onboarding milestones. I attached a lightly redlined SOW and a proposed acceptance checklist.

Next steps: Marissa, can you confirm commission % visibility in our RevOps flows and any constraints on milestone invoices? Camila / Karthik — can we confirm the integration test expectations?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Remarks_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Ellen Harper <ellen.harper@skyline-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partner rev-share discussion: integration milestones & lead pathing

Neha / Camila / Ellen — running numbers from a RevOps perspective:

- Commission math: the 60/40 proposal from Skyline is fine as a starting point. For clarity I suggest we map to net-new ARR after discounts and marketplace fees. Redwood will generate a monthly partner revenue report and pay quarterly.
- Milestone invoicing: Redwood finance can accept milestone invoices but needs PO references and a consolidated quarterly invoice for disbursement. For accounting reasons, we prefer milestone recognition on completion dates rather than upfront cash-outflows in an earlier period.
- Lead validation: we'll require a HubSpot registration ID + one supporting artifact (intro email thread or signed LOI). The lead-registration-matrix.xlsx Ellen attached is a good start; I'll add a column for HubSpot ID and CRM opportunity owner.

Edge cases / exceptions:
- If Skyline re-engages a Redwood-won customer to upsell, that uplift is Redwood-owned (no rev-share).
- If a customer converts after >90 days but the intro can be shown via tracked nurtures, we can escalate to a credit review.

Ellen — if the above is acceptable I'll convert this into a short Partner Payment Addendum for legal to attach to the SOW.

—Marissa
Sr. Partner Ops Manager | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Ellen Harper <ellen.harper@skyline-analytics.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partner rev-share discussion: integration milestones & lead pathing

Thanks all — technical clarifications from infra/integration:

- Integration acceptance: Skyline's idea of using an automated integration harness is great. Proposed gating: (a) run the agreed test suite against a staging instance for 72 hours with <1% error on representative payloads, (b) KV cache warmup and sample-latency targets must be met with the expected token mix (we'll share a sample profile), and (c) data handling/compliance checklist (GDPR/data residency if EU customers are in scope).
- API versioning & rollouts: we need to pin the model+runtime config for the pilot to avoid regressions. Any model upgrades after go-live will require change-control and 30-day notice to Skyline to avoid impacting SLA.
- Sandbox for integrations: Redwood can provision a sandbox with limited throughput for CI runs — we'll require a signed sandbox access agreement (simple NDA + acceptable use).

I'll draft a one-page Technical Acceptance Appendix and share by COB Monday. If the partner agrees to the 72-hour staging run and sandbox NDA, we can lock milestone 2 (integration complete).

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
